title: Node2Shell: Brotli Flaw Hits Python Packages
content_md: The Node2Shell Brotli flaw (CVE-2026-111497), disclosed alongside Node.js fixes on October 21, 2026, also reaches Python through the PyPI Brotli and brotlicffi packages. Both compile Google’s vulnerable Brotli C decoder, and popular HTTP clients such as requests, httpx and aiohttp use them to decompress responses automatically once they are installed. That makes exposure easy to miss. A Python service can hand attacker-controlled Brotli data to the decoder without a single Brotli import in its own code. No exploitation in the wild has been reported, but researchers have already shown Remote Code Execution (RCE) against Node.js through the same decoder code, so Python teams should move to the fixed versions, Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0, without waiting.
